title: Sin as death; grace vivifies with Christ (Eph 2; Col 2)
source_text: XIV. Verum Scriptura de peccato non loquitur simpliciter tanquam de morbo, sive infirmitate, sed etiam tanquam de morte, in qua sine Dei gratia jacemus, & a qua per illam excitamur, & in novam vitam resurgimus. Nam, ut ait Apostolus, Deus qui dives est in misericordia, quum essemus mortui in peccatis, convivificavit nos Christo, cujus gratia estis salvati. Eph. 2. & similiter Col. 2. Vos, inquit, cum mortui essetis in delictis convivificavit cum illo. Et antea dixerat fideles in baptismo Christo consépultos, simul cum illo resurgere.
pass_a_gloss: But Scripture does not speak of sin simply as of a disease or infirmity, but also as of a death in which without God's grace we lie, and from which by it we are raised and rise into new life. For, as the Apostle says, God who is rich in mercy, when we were dead in sins, made us alive together with Christ, by whose grace you are saved (Ephesians 2); and likewise Colossians 2: You, he says, when you were dead in trespasses, he made alive together with him. And earlier he had said that the faithful, buried with Christ in baptism, rise together with him.
pass_b_english: Sin is also death; grace raises us into new life with Christ (Ephesians 2; Colossians 2).
Baptismal burial with Christ means rising with him.
